citation_with_page: Federal Reserve discount and funds-rate series (FRED FEDFUNDS from 1954-07; discount rate 1.5 to 3.5 percent Aug 1955-Aug 1957, recalled); NBER reference peak Aug 1957 (nber.org/research/data/us-business-cycle-expansions-and-contractions, page n/a; the cycle dating is the builder judgment)
FRED FEDFUNDS (0.93 percent Jun 1958 to 3.99 percent Dec 1959, read this session); NBER reference peak Apr 1960 (same NBER table; cycle dating is the builder judgment)

FRED FEDFUNDS (3.90 percent Jan 1965 to 5.40 percent Dec 1966, read this session); no NBER peak within 24 months of Dec 1966, next peak Dec 1969 (same NBER table); credit crunch of 1966 produced a growth slowdown, not a dated recession
FRED FEDFUNDS (3.98 percent Jun 1967 to 8.97 percent Dec 1969, read this session); NBER reference peak Dec 1969 (same NBER table)
FRED FEDFUNDS (3.51 percent Jan 1972 to 9.95 percent Dec 1973, read this session); NBER reference peak Nov 1973 (same NBER table); the recession began before the funds rate peaked in Jul 1974

BLS CPI-U Dec/Dec via FRED CPIAUCNS (read this session): 1945 2.2 percent, 1946 18.1 percent after OPA controls lapsed in 1946; rule: inflation in the year after controls end no higher than in the final controlled year
FRED CPIAUCNS (read this session): 1952 0.8 percent (final controlled year), 1953 0.7 percent after Economic Stabilization Agency controls ended in early 1953 (end date recalled, primary not seen)
FRED CPIAUCNS (read this session): 1973 8.7 percent, 1974 12.3 percent after Phase IV controls lapsed Apr 1974 (date recalled; Kosters 1975 AEI retrospective, primary not seen, pages not verified)

FRED CPIAUCNS (read this session): year-on-year CPI 8.9 percent Oct 1978 (guidelines announced 1978-10-24, recalled) to 11.8 percent Aug 1979; guidelines still in force so the trial is read at the last CPI published before the decision
